body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat L=L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\). The numerically explicit no-MOT rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) and the theoretically calibrated rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\), for a finite \(C_d\) established to exist by the plug-in theorem, both belong to \(\mathcal H_\alpha\). The proved bounds are \(c_d\max\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\}\le R_d(N,K)\le C_d[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\) and \(c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\le C_{d,\alpha}[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\). Consequently both risks are of order \(N^{-1/2}\) when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\); exact functions \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}\) remain unresolved on the residual small-ratio arrays.

sampling_model.design: Balanced \(K=K_N\)-arm product experiment with \(N=Km\) and fixed \(d>4\).
sampling_model.units: For arm \(k\), \(X_{k1},\ldots,X_{km}\) are identically distributed from the arbitrary marginal \(P_k\) on \(\mathbb B_d\); all arm samples are independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed experiment supplies one independent sample from each potential-outcome marginal and leaves the within-unit \(K\)-world coupling unidentified.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each marginal is estimated empirically. No density, smoothness, joint-mixability, known nuisance, or centered-variance substitution is imposed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published model permits all dimensions and \(K\ge2\). On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap, its arbitrary marginal class is the same \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and its balanced i.i.d. unit sampling induces the armwise product law used here; Theorem 1 gives \(N^{-1/2}+\min\{K^{-1},K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\}\).
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The improved plug-in theorem strictly tightens that common-overlap display, the dimension-dependent theorem proves the sharper \(q_d\) root-\(N\) elbow, the mean-only corollaries retain a separate no-MOT baseline, and the STAR proposition audits the additional scaling and subsampling needed for the application.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.6 places a binary covariate-aware mirror-transport lower bound between unconditional and conditional transport, while Theorem 4.3 gives its quadratic-cost plug-in rate under smooth strongly convex Brenier potentials.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The residual frontier question concerns unconditional arbitrary margins with growing \(K\) and is informed by, but does not claim to extend, this binary covariate-aware result.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper proves continuity of binary conditional transport under adapted Wasserstein distance and derives a direct nonparametric estimator with a convergence rate.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The residual frontier question is only informed by this conditional binary theory.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper gives a smooth-density wavelet estimator and asymptotic normality for binary conditional transport with quadratic cost.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The residual frontier question imposes no density smoothness and records this result only as context.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 22 gives the two-margin all-estimator lower bound \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) for quadratic cost.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The known sandwich embeds this as a two-margin subclass, so its lower bound transfers upward to the arbitrary-margin class; the residual question does not claim that this settles the missing arm factor or the logarithm.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.2 converts binary \(c\)-transform entropy into two-margin empirical transport rates.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The joint-dual-complexity question asks whether an aggregate analogue exists for a growing tuple of jointly conjugate potentials.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives uniformly valid one-sided inference from a dual-feasible estimated pair in randomized experiments.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The explicit mean-floor theorem gives a no-MOT honest baseline, while the plug-in honest-length theorem gives a sharper theoretical rate with an existential calibration constant; neither is advertised as a numerically explicit dual-feasible implementation of the comparator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper constructs finite-sample intervals for sliced Wasserstein distance and bounds their length near the minimax rate.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The mean-floor and plug-in theorems address one-sided excess length for the multiworld endpoint, with matching order proved only in their respective root-\(N\) regions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper gives necessary and sufficient joint-mixability conditions for selected classes of univariate distributions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The sharp residual-envelope theorem treats arbitrary heterogeneous vector marginals and uses this literature only as context.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Donsker dual classes yield two-margin empirical optimal-transport limits given by suprema of Gaussian processes.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The joint-dual-complexity question asks for the distinct growing-arm high-dimensional aggregate bound.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Upper and lower Wasserstein dimensions determine multiscale empirical-measure approximation rates.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The residual frontier question concerns a smooth multi-marginal value rather than empirical-measure approximation itself.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Quadratic negative-dependence objectives are optimized for selected identical scalar margins admitting a joint mix.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The sharp residual-envelope theorem allows arbitrary heterogeneous vector margins and does not claim an extension of the selected scalar characterization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The ordered modulus gives one-sided minimax expected-length optimality for linear Gaussian regression functionals.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The ordered low-versus-high requirement in the residual frontier question uses this only as decision-theoretic motivation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Optimal multi-margin dual potentials may be chosen as a simultaneously conjugate family.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The joint-dual-complexity question asks for a statistical aggregate bound not supplied by dual attainment alone.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Two-mode stability controls regular Monge maps for barycentric and uniformly concave sum costs.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The joint-dual-complexity question instead retains arbitrary margins and the repulsive squared-sum endpoint.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Fixed-finite-support multi-sample optimal-transport values admit weak limits and bootstrap tests.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The rational family in the residual question is a finite certificate handle, not a claim that fixed-support asymptotics settle the arbitrary-margin frontier.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sharp two-arm randomization-variance bounds yield asymptotically conservative narrow Wald intervals under unequal allocation.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The STAR proposition is a conditional balanced-subsampling audit and does not claim the comparator's unequal-allocation result for three margins.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Generic discrete multimarginal transport approximation has exponential tensor dependence in the number of margins.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The certified computation theorem exploits fixed-dimensional partial-sum structure and promises polynomial dependence on \((K/\epsilon)^d\), not generic exact transport complexity.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Generic pairwise-interaction multimarginal transport is computationally hard.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The certified computation theorem is restricted to the squared-sum cost and fixed dimension and therefore does not contradict the generic hardness result.

body.tldr: The target \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp causal second moment compatible with the observed potential-outcome marginals, not a centered variance residual. On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced arbitrary-margin class, the core sharpens Gao--Ge--Qian's empirical upper rate through the exact residual envelope and optimal-sum geometry. Matching root-\(N\) orders for minimax estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length are proved only when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\); the exact smaller-arm frontier remains open, including irregular arrays with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\), fixed-\(K\) logarithms, and the ordered converse. The mean-floor lower bound is a separate numerically explicit no-MOT procedure and yields its own root-\(N\) baseline for \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\). The sharper plug-in lower bound is uniformly honest for a finite constant \(C_d\) proved to exist, but it is a theoretical calibration rather than a directly reportable numerical rule. The rational primal--dual procedure certifies the empirical MOT value to requested numerical width; it does not supply that statistical constant. The finite simultaneous-marginal template is defined but not instantiated. The STAR audit remains conditional on a known finite outcome bound, affine scaling, an i.i.d. superpopulation law, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling, and does not validate the native \(161/37/36\) calculation.

project_justification.gap: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class, Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1 has high-dimensional term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\), while their Proposition 2 prints a two-margin lower expression with \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) and supplies neither uniform one-sided coverage nor minimax expected excess length. Their published scope is broader in dimension and includes \(K=2\), but on this overlap both papers allow the same arbitrary laws in \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and their balanced i.i.d. setup induces this note's armwise product experiment. The embedded Manole--Niles-Weed lower bound is valid on a two-margin subclass and therefore transfers upward, but it does not settle the missing arm factor or fixed-\(K\) logarithm. The exact estimation and ordered one-sided frontiers remain unresolved precisely on subsequences where \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\), including those inside irregular arrays.
project_justification.niche: The squared-sum cost has shared fixed-dimensional geometry: all dual potentials obey one joint constraint, and optimal coupling atoms admit arbitrary-subset exchanges. A valid lower construction must nevertheless survive every alternative multi-arm rematching. The paper therefore separates three deliverables: a numerically explicit mean-only confidence floor, sharper theoretical plug-in rates, and a finite rational certificate handle for the unresolved simultaneous perturbation problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp deterministic residual and support-diameter results, a tighter empirical plug-in upper bound, the dimension-dependent root-\(N\) elbow, matching root-\(N\) one-sided expected-length order in that region, an independently useful mean-floor no-MOT baseline, and a rational primal--dual bracket for the empirical endpoint. The theoretical plug-in confidence rule uses a finite \(C_d\) established to exist and is not called numerically explicit. The finite-support perturbation template is defined but not instantiated: endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, resistance to every rematching column with strict off-contact slack, and the ordered low-versus-high separation remain explicit targets. The residual question covers every legal array not eventually bounded below by a positive multiple of \(N^{q_d}\) through its small-ratio subsequences. The STAR audit separately declares the known bound, affine scale, superpopulation law, complete randomization, and balanced subsampling required for its conditional application statement.

body.related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define the same second-moment endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) and treat a published class covering all dimensions and \(K\ge2\). On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap, their distributional class is the same arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and their balanced i.i.d. unit design induces the armwise product law used here. Their Theorem 1 gives the displayed empirical upper rate, while their high-dimensional minimax claim remains open. This core's sharper plug-in theorem and \(q_d\) elbow are comparisons only on that common class. Its mean-floor theorems are an independent, numerically explicit no-MOT route, not the sharp elbow. Manole and Niles-Weed provide the closest all-estimator lower architecture for quadratic two-margin transport. Because the two-margin construction is a subclass of the arbitrary-margin model, its lower bound transfers upward, but its \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) order does not close the multi-arm gap. Binary covariate-aware transport results of Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn inform the causal framing but impose a different conditional structure and do not settle this unconditional growing-arm endpoint. Two-margin entropy transfer and Donsker results of Hundrieser and coauthors do not control an increasing jointly conjugate tuple. Work on vector mixability, selected scalar joint mixes, regular Monge stability, multiscale Wasserstein approximation, sliced-Wasserstein intervals, dual-feasible causal inference, and ordered moduli supplies neighboring geometry or inference tools but not the missing all-rematching simultaneous family or shared-dual aggregate bound. The finite-support MOT literature motivates the rational diagnostic but does not establish its required separation. The certified algorithm exploits the present fixed-dimensional squared-sum structure and is consistent with generic multimarginal hardness results. Gao--Ge--Qian's STAR application uses native cell sizes \(161,37,36\); the conditional audit here requires a known finite bound, affine rescaling, an i.i.d. superpopulation law, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling and does not reproduce the native unequal-count tightening.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved class consists of every legal array with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\). A complete answer must work on every further subsequence where the ratio tends to zero and splice consistently with root-\(N\) subsequences, so oscillatory arrays cannot be removed by assuming a full-sequence limit. The known nonparametric lower term is \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\), whereas the proved upper term may retain \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\). The finite-support perturbation template has not been instantiated with endpoint separation, mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and positive reduced-cost slack off every declared contact set; tensoring two-margin, parity, or orthogonal gadgets fails because alternative arms may rematch. No sharper aggregate theorem for the jointly conjugate potentials is known. The plug-in confidence rule is uniformly honest only after choosing a finite theorem constant \(C_d\); absent its numerical value, the rule is theoretical rather than directly reportable. The mean-floor rule remains explicit and avoids MOT but has the coarser residual term \(r/K^2\). The certified computation theorem brackets only the empirical endpoint, is fixed-dimensional, and has polynomial dependence on \((K/\epsilon)^d\), not a generic exact-MOT guarantee. The STAR audit discards observations, depends on the declared known-bound superpopulation model, and does not reproduce the published native-cell computation.
body.honest_scope: The note fixes \(d>4\), assumes balanced armwise product sampling with \(K\ge3\) and \(m=N/K\to\infty\), allows arbitrary unit-ball marginals, and preserves the uncentered second-moment endpoint \(L\). The sharp residual envelope, support diameter, improved empirical upper bound, decision-risk sandwiches, dimension-dependent root-\(N\) frontier, theoretical plug-in honesty result, explicit mean-floor corollaries, numerical certificate, parity witness, and conditional STAR audit are established only under their displayed assumptions. Matching root-\(N\) estimation and one-sided expected-length orders are claimed only for \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), with \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The mean-only no-MOT route independently gives a coarser root-\(N\) baseline when \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\). The plug-in lower bound is a theoretical uniformly calibrated rule because its \(C_d\) is existential; only the mean-floor formula and the empirical MOT numerical bracket are directly computable from the stated information. No exact rate or ordered nonparametric length converse is claimed on small-ratio subsequences, and the simultaneous family is only a construction handle. The two-margin specialization is a definitional reduction and supplies a subclass converse, not a full multi-arm lower construction. The hypercube statement includes the legal \(K=3,d=5\) value \(1/9\). The STAR conclusion applies only after the declared scaling and randomized balanced subsampling and makes no claim for the native unequal cell counts.
